sections.title: Solomon
sections.description: Solomon's reign and the building of the temple

sections.title: The Early Kings
sections.description: From the division of the kingdom to Jehoshaphat

sections.title: The Final Kings
sections.description: From Manasseh to the fall of Jerusalem

events.title: Solomon's Wisdom
events.description: Solomon goes to the high place at Gibeon and offers a thousand burnt offerings. During the night God appears to him and tells him to ask for whatever he wants. Solomon asks for wisdom and knowledge to lead the people, and God grants this to him, along with riches, wealth, and honor such as no king before or after him has had.

events.title: The Building of the Temple Begins
events.description: Solomon begins building the house of the Lord on Mount Moriah in Jerusalem, at the place David had prepared. He sends word to King Hiram of Tyre for cedar and cypress timber and skilled craftsmen. The construction work starts in his fourth year as king.

events.title: Temple Equipment
events.description: Solomon makes the bronze altar, the cast sea resting on twelve bronze bulls, ten golden lampstands, ten tables, one hundred gold bowls, and the two large pillars, Jakin and Boaz, in front of the temple. Huram-Abi carries out the skilled bronze work.

events.title: The Ark of the Covenant is Moved to the Temple
events.description: The priests and Levites carry the Ark of the Covenant into the Most Holy Place in the temple. When the priests go out, a cloud fills the house of the Lord, so that the priests cannot stand and serve, for the glory of the Lord fills the house of God.

events.title: The Temple is Dedicated
events.description: Solomon offers a long dedication prayer before the altar with his hands raised toward heaven. He asks God to hear the people's prayers when they turn toward this house. When he finishes, fire falls from heaven and consumes the burnt offering, and the glory of the Lord fills the house. The dedication festival lasts for fourteen days.

events.title: God's Promise and Warning to Solomon
events.description: The Lord appears to Solomon at night and says that He has heard his prayer and chosen this house as a place of sacrifice. God gives the famous promise: "If my people humble themselves and pray, I will hear from heaven and heal their land." But He also warns that disobedience will lead to the temple being abandoned.

events.title: The Queen of Sheba Visits Solomon
events.description: The Queen of Sheba comes to test Solomon with difficult questions. She is overwhelmed by his wisdom, his palace, the food at his table, the conduct of his servants, and his burnt offerings in the house of the Lord. She declares that not even half had been told her, and gives him large amounts of gold, spices, and precious stones.

events.title: Solomon's Wealth and Greatness
events.description: Solomon surpasses all the kings of the earth in wealth and wisdom. He receives 666 talents of gold annually, makes two hundred large and three hundred small gold shields, and a great ivory throne. Silver was as common as stone in Jerusalem during his time.

events.title: The Kingdom Divides
events.description: After Solomon's death, Rehoboam goes to Shechem to be crowned. The people ask for relief from the heavy burdens Solomon placed on them. Rehoboam rejects the advice of the elders and follows the harsh approach of the young men. The ten northern tribes revolt under Jeroboam, and only Judah and Benjamin remain under Rehoboam.

events.title: Shishak's Invasion
events.description: Because Rehoboam and Judah have abandoned the law of the Lord, Pharaoh Shishak of Egypt marches against Jerusalem with 1,200 chariots and 60,000 horsemen. The prophet Shemaiah explains that this happens because they left the Lord. The kings humble themselves, and the Lord spares them from complete destruction, but Shishak takes the treasures from the temple and the royal palace.

events.title: Asa's Reform
events.description: King Asa removes foreign altars and high places, breaks down sacred pillars, and cuts down Asherah poles. He commands Judah to seek the Lord and keep the law. When the Cushite Zerah advances against him with an army of a million men, Asa cries out to the Lord, and God defeats the enemy. The prophet Azariah encourages him, and Asa renews the covenant with the Lord.

events.title: Jehoshaphat's Reign
events.description: Jehoshaphat walks in the ways of the Lord, sends out leaders and Levites to teach the people the law, and appoints judges in all the fortified cities of Judah. The Lord is with him, and neighboring nations fear going to war against Judah. He strengthens the land and builds up a mighty army.

events.title: Jehoshaphat's Victory over Moab and Ammon
events.description: A large army of Moabites, Ammonites, and Meunites marches against Judah. Jehoshaphat proclaims a fast throughout the land and prays to the Lord in the temple. The Levite Jahaziel prophesies that the battle is God's, not theirs. The next day, Jehoshaphat sends praise singers ahead of the army, and the Lord sets ambushes against the enemies, causing them to destroy each other. Judah spends three days gathering the plunder.

events.title: Athaliah and Joash
events.description: After Ahaziah's death, his mother Athaliah seizes power and kills the entire royal family. But Jehosheba, Ahaziah's sister, hides the young Joash in the temple for six years. In the seventh year, the priest Jehoiada organizes a coup, anoints Joash as king, and executes Athaliah. Jehoiada renews the covenant between the Lord, the king, and the people.

events.title: The Temple Restored under Joash
events.description: Joash decides to repair the house of the Lord. He places a chest at the entrance to the temple, and the people willingly bring offerings. The money is used to pay stonecutters, carpenters, and other craftsmen who restore the temple to its original condition and make it stronger than before.

events.title: Uzziah's Rise and Fall
events.description: Uzziah becomes king at sixteen years old and reigns for 52 years. As long as he seeks the Lord, God gives him success. He builds towers, digs wells, and maintains a large army. But when he becomes powerful, his heart grows proud. He enters the temple to burn incense, something only priests are allowed to do. The priests confront him, and God strikes him with leprosy, which he carries until the day of his death.

events.title: Hezekiah's Reforms
events.description: Already in his first month as king, Hezekiah opens the doors to the house of the Lord and sets the priests and Levites to work cleansing the temple. He restores worship with music and praise, and invites all Israel and Judah to celebrate Passover in Jerusalem. It becomes the greatest Passover celebration since the days of Solomon. Afterwards, the people go out and destroy the idols and high places throughout the land.

events.title: Sennacherib's Siege of Jerusalem
events.description: The Assyrian king Sennacherib invades Judah and besieges the fortified cities. Hezekiah prepares the defense and blocks up the water sources outside the city. Sennacherib sends mocking messages and tries to frighten the people. Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah pray to the Lord, and the Lord sends an angel who strikes down 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp. Sennacherib is forced to retreat in shame and is killed by his own sons.

events.title: Manasseh's Captivity and Repentance
events.description: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned for 55 years. He rebuilt the high places, set up altars to Baal, worshipped the host of heaven, and made his son pass through fire. The Lord warned him, but he did not listen. The king of Assyria captured him with hooks and brought him to Babylon in bronze chains. In his distress, Manasseh humbled himself deeply and prayed to the Lord, who heard him and brought him back to Jerusalem. Then Manasseh understood that the Lord is God.

events.title: Josiah's Reforms
events.description: Josiah became king at eight years old, and in his eighth year he began to seek the Lord. In his twelfth year, he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem of high places, Asherah poles, and carved images. During the restoration of the temple, the priest Hilkiah found the Book of the Law. When Josiah heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes in grief because the people had not kept the Lord's word.

events.title: Josiah's Passover Celebration
events.description: Josiah holds a great Passover celebration in Jerusalem. More than 30,000 lambs and goats are slaughtered from the king's own property, and the leaders give generously to the people and the priests. The book of Chronicles says such a Passover has not been held in Israel since the days of the prophet Samuel. The Levites serve with music as David had established.

events.title: The Fall of Jerusalem
events.description: King Zedekiah does what is evil in the Lord's eyes and refuses to humble himself before the prophet Jeremiah. All the leaders and the people are unfaithful and defile themselves with the abominations of the nations. The Lord sends message after message through His prophets, but they mock the messengers, despise God's word, and ridicule the prophets until the Lord's wrath becomes unavoidable. The Chaldeans burn God's house, tear down Jerusalem's walls, and take the people into exile in Babylon.

events.title: Cyrus's decree
events.description: The Persian Cyrus conquers Babylon, and in his first year he issues a decree fulfilling Jeremiah's prophecy: The Lord has given him all the kingdoms of the earth, and he commands his people to allow the Jews to return to Jerusalem to build the house of the Lord. This declaration ends 2 Chronicles with a glimpse of hope after the exile.
